title: Preface
summary: The partial document covers the Bluefin Sound Fisheries Cooperative's Quota and Harvest Report for 2025. It includes sections on the cooperative's overview, fleet composition, catch quotas for 2025, sustainability measures, processing and markets, and an outlook for 2026.

title: Cooperative Overview
summary:
The main points covered in the partial document are:
- The cooperative's founding in 1957 by 22 fishing families
- Headquarters in the port of Bluefin Sound, Nova Scotia
- Membership growth to 118 member vessels by the end of 2025
- Management of quotas, operation of the fuel dock, and running the processing plant
- A board of seven elected skippers that meets every second Thursday

title: Fleet Composition
summary: The main points covered in the partial document are the composition of the member fleet, the average vessel age, recent fleet renewals, and the equipment of new vessels.

title: Catch Quotas 2025
summary: The partial document discusses the 2025 catch quotas and actual landings for various fish species. It highlights that herring was fully utilized, while pollock remained below quota due to a shift in the fleet's effort towards haddock. No quotas were exceeded. The document also provides a table comparing the allocated quotas with the actual landings for Atlantic cod, haddock, pollock, herring, and halibut.

title: Sustainability Measures
summary: The partial document covers sustainability measures including closed areas to protect juvenile cod, changes in mesh size for trawl fishing, independent observer coverage, and a discard monitoring program involving deck cameras.

title: Processing and Markets
summary: The partial document covers the processing and market aspects of a fishing operation. Key points include the capacity and recent processing volume of a plant on the east quay, export data for 2025, and price information for cod. Additionally, it mentions the primary market for herring.

title: Outlook 2026
summary: The partial document covers proposals for the 2026 season, including a 3 percent reduction in the cod quota, an unchanged herring quota, and a request for a pollock assessment review. It also mentions fleet renewal with nine additional vessels ordered for 2026 and 2027, and plans for heat recovery from the refrigeration system to be connected to the fuel dock building in spring 2026.
